doc: The settlement config a plan system is bound to (design/planner.md, Scenarios): the scenario and its ranges, the ground it is laid on, its roads, plot classes and shapes, waterfronts, open bodies, walls, and water; and the lots its building and waterfront plots are made of.

fields.name: scenario
fields.doc: How the settlement is laid out (a castle: a curtain wall round an outer ward, and the keep's ward inside its own wall).

fields.name: plots_min
fields.doc: The fewest household plots at its final tier.

fields.name: plots_max
fields.doc: The most household plots at its final tier.

fields.name: density
fields.doc: Cells of working ground per plot cell (2 a tight town, 4 a loose hamlet); the village takes only the shape it grows into.

fields.name: terrain
fields.doc: The natural ground before levelling.

fields.name: relief_m
fields.doc: The natural ground's height range, metres.

fields.name: feature_cells
fields.doc: The size of the ground's hills and hollows, cells.

fields.name: entrances
fields.doc: How many roads come in (a walled town's gates).

fields.name: high_width
fields.doc: The high street's width, cells (1 to 3).

fields.name: lane_width
fields.doc: A lane's width, cells (1 or 2).

fields.name: high_grade
fields.doc: The steepest a high street climbs (rise over run): a cart's limit.

fields.name: lane_grade
fields.doc: The steepest a lane climbs.

fields.name: block_cells
fields.doc: How far back lanes run behind the streets they parallel, cells (about two plot depths; 12 for burgages).

fields.name: alley_every
fields.doc: Cells between alleys that cut through long blocks (0: none).

fields.name: square_cells
fields.doc: The main node's radius, cells: a crossroads (0 or 1), a square, or the open body's size.

fields.name: centre
fields.doc: A centre at the square's middle (a well, a market cross, a fountain: a civic building on a centre lot), the square's road ringing it.

fields.name: open_body
fields.doc: What the village gathers round: nothing, a green (open land the plotter fills), a pond, or a lake (with waterfronts on its shore).

fields.name: margin_cells
fields.doc: Open land kept round the village's plots and roads, cells: its gardens and backs, which pass to the plotter.

fields.name: share_solo
fields.doc: The share of plots for one person.

fields.name: share_family
fields.doc: The share of plots for a family.

fields.name: share_extended
fields.doc: The share of plots for several generations.

fields.name: civic
fields.doc: Civic plots (the temple, a guild hall) at the final tier.

fields.name: crop_fields
fields.doc: Crop field plots beside the farms, at most.

fields.name: keep_ward_cells
fields.doc: The keep's ward: its radius in cells, inside its own wall with a gate, holding the keep and the castle's parts round a bailey (0: none).

fields.name: castle_parts
fields.doc: Castle parts in the keep's ward besides the keep (a great hall, a chapel, barracks, stables, a kitchen, storehouses).

fields.name: outer_parts
fields.doc: Castle parts in a castle's outer ward (barracks, stables, storehouses), beside its households.

fields.name: waterfronts
fields.doc: Waterfront plots (piers, boathouses, warehouses, fisheries) along its water, at most.

fields.name: halves_market
fields.doc: How many market cells get an edge piece in a half (a stall), 0 to 1; the plan keeps every way through open.

fields.name: halves_square
fields.doc: How many square cells get an edge piece in a half, 0 to 1.

fields.name: halves_high
fields.doc: How many high-street cells beside a front get one, 0 to 1.

fields.name: halves_lane
fields.doc: How many lane cells beside a building get one, 0 to 1.

fields.name: halves_quay
fields.doc: How many quay cells get one (crates, carts), 0 to 1.

fields.name: fence_share
fields.doc: The share of household plots whose yard is fenced, 0 to 1.

fields.name: fence_cells
fields.doc: How far a fenced yard reaches from its plot, cells.

fields.name: shape_wide
fields.doc: How often a plot is wide.

fields.name: shape_deep
fields.doc: How often a plot is deep.

fields.name: shape_round
fields.doc: How often a plot is round.

fields.name: shape_long
fields.doc: How often a plot is long (a burgage).

fields.name: shape_broad
fields.doc: How often a plot is broad (a shopfront).

fields.name: walls
fields.doc: What rings the settlement: wall cells in a line with gates where roads cross (the game's wall_v1 kind follows the material).

fields.name: wall_reach_cells
fields.doc: How far a wall reaches out round what's built, cells: the wall follows a metaball of the plots and squares (smooth, never nearer a building than a cell).

fields.name: river
fields.doc: A river crosses the site, bridged where a road meets it.

fields.name: river_cells
fields.doc: The river's width, cells.

fields.name: lot_class
fields.doc: Each lot's size class: 0 solo, 1 family, 2 extended, 3 civic, 4 castle, 5 waterfront, 6 centre, 7 field (plan_v1_plot's size_class).

fields.name: lot_shape
fields.doc: Each lot's shape: 0 wide, 1 deep, 2 round, 3 long, 4 broad (plan_v1_plot's shape; a civic or castle lot's is its order by size, smallest first).

fields.name: lot_cells
fields.doc: Each lot's cells: lot, q, r triples (axial, pointy-top, 1 m cells), relative to the cell its anchor (and a building's origin) is on, facing +z.

fields.name: lot_wet
fields.doc: Which lots' cells must be water: lot, q, r triples (a waterfront's, +z the water).

fields.name: lot_doors
fields.doc: Each lot's door cells (outside its front): lot, q, r triples, relative to its anchor, facing +z. A lot is placed only where one of them is a road.
